feed.title: Polar Star Project: alerts from the records

entry.title: ICE has not posted its required detention statistics
entry.summary: ICE's last detention statistics file is dated July 20, 2026: 98 days with no new file when ICE's page was checked on October 26, 2026. Congress asked for this file every two weeks, so about 7 updates have been missed. The requirement was added in the fiscal 2020 DHS appropriations law; reporting has noted debate over whether it still binds ICE.

entry.title: Share of people in ICE detention held more than a year
entry.summary: 4,161 people in ICE detention on August 6, 2026 had been held more than a year, and 12,736 more than six months (6.3% and 19.3% of the 65,890 held). Long stays often come from cases still before a judge or on appeal, which can take more than a year. ICE's records do not say why any one stay has lasted this long, whether it has been reviewed, or whether the person has a final removal order. ICE's own twice-monthly file gives a lower figure, 2,112 held more than a year on June 30, 2026. This count runs from the start of each continuous stay in ICE detention, across transfers; ICE's file does not say how it measures, so the two are not directly comparable. For people with a final removal order, the Supreme Court set six months as the presumptively reasonable limit when removal is not reasonably foreseeable (Zadvydas v. Davis, 2001). The records cannot show how many of these stays that applies to; that is the question for the bodies below.

entry.title: Adams County Correctional Center: share held more than a year well above other facilities
entry.summary: 422 of the 2,415 people held here on August 6, 2026 had been in ICE detention more than a year (17%), against 6.3% of everyone held. At the national share, a count this high would come up by chance less than once in 100. Long stays often come from cases still in court or on appeal; the records do not say which.

entry.title: Adelanto ICE Processing Center: deaths well above other facilities
entry.summary: 4 deaths ICE reported here from August 2025 to July 2026: 24.4 for every 10,000 people held for a year, against 6.2 across all facilities on ICE's list over the same months. At the overall rate, a count this high would come up by chance about 2 times in 100. Officials were refused entry here 1 time since August 2025. This is listed beside the figures above as a fact; it does not show that one caused the other. About 1,635 people a day were held here from August 2025 to July 2026. Rates from a handful of deaths move a lot with one event.

entry.title: Lawsuit, Illinois, IL (2025-12-22)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued Illinois over two 2025 state laws, the Illinois Bivens Act and the Courts Access, Safety, and Participation Act (United States v. Illinois, S.D. Ill.). Latest on record (2026-10-16): The court denied Illinois's motion to dismiss and set a bench trial for January 24, 2028. Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-sues-jb-pritzker-kwame-raoul-over-illinois-bivens-act

entry.title: Lawsuit, New York City, NY (2025-07-24)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued New York City over its laws that limit city help with federal immigration enforcement (United States v. City of New York, E.D.N.Y.). Latest on record (2026-10-16): The court dismissed the case and entered judgment for the city. Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-sues-new-york-city-over-sanctuary-policies

entry.title: Lawsuit, California, CA (2026-10-15)
entry.summary: California sued DHS and ICE over ICE's courthouse enforcement directive and civil immigration arrests at California courthouses (C.D. Cal.). Source: https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/100-lawsuits-21-months-attorney-general-bonta-sues-ice-over-civil-immigration

entry.title: Lawsuit, Baltimore, MD (2026-03-10)
entry.summary: Maryland sued ICE and DHS to force production of the records ICE had refused to provide (Maryland v. Lyons, D. Md.). Latest on record (2026-10-15): The court dismissed the case without prejudice, holding that the state law does not authorize subpoenas to federal agencies. Source: https://oag.maryland.gov/News/Pages/Attorney-General-Brown-Files-Lawsuit-to-Force-ICE-to-Turn-Over-Records-for-OAG%E2%80%99s-Civil-Rights-Investigation-into-Reported-D.aspx

entry.title: Lawsuit, California, CA (2025-11-17)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued California over two 2025 laws that limit face coverings for officers and require them to show identification (United States v. California, C.D. Cal.). Latest on record (2026-10-14): The Ninth Circuit reversed the district court's refusal to block the identification requirement and told it to issue a preliminary injunction against that requirement. Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-files-complaint-challenging-california-mask-ban-and-identification

entry.title: Criminal charge, Minneapolis, MN (2026-04-16)
entry.summary: The Hennepin County Attorney charged an ICE officer with two counts of second-degree assault for allegedly pointing his weapon at two people in a car on Highway 62 on February 5, 2026. Latest on record (2026-10-13): The case is in state court; a federal judge has not ruled on the request to move it to federal court. Source: https://www.hennepinattorney.org/news/news/2026/April/morgan-charges

entry.title: Lawsuit, 21 states and the District of Columbia, led by New Jersey, NJ (2025-08-18)
entry.summary: States sued the Justice Department over conditions on crime-victim grants that required them to help DHS with civil immigration enforcement; amended complaints added Byrne JAG and other grant conditions (New Jersey v. DOJ, D.R.I.). Latest on record (2026-10-08): Both sides have asked the court to decide the case without trial; no ruling yet. Source: https://www.wisdoj.gov/PressReleases/8-18-2025-VOCA-Multistate.pdf

entry.title: Lawsuit, Newark, Jersey City, Paterson and Hoboken, NJ (2025-05-22)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued four New Jersey cities over policies that limit city help with federal immigration enforcement (United States v. City of Newark, D.N.J.). Latest on record (2026-10-06): The court entered final judgment dismissing the case without prejudice and closed it. Source: https://clearinghouse.net/case/46729/

entry.title: Lawsuit, Maine, ME (2026-05-27)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued Maine over a state policy that denies confidential license plates to federal agencies, including ICE; it filed similar suits against three other states the same day. Latest on record (2026-09-22): Maine moved to dismiss; the motion was fully briefed on September 22, 2026, and no ruling is on record. Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-sues-states-denying-undercover-license-plates-federal-law-enforcement

entry.title: Criminal charge, North Minneapolis, MN (2026-05-18)
entry.summary: The Hennepin County Attorney charged an ICE officer with four counts of second-degree assault and one count of falsely reporting a crime over a January 14, 2026 shooting through a home's front door that wounded a man. Latest on record (2026-09-17): He made a first appearance in state court and was released on bail. Source: https://www.hennepinattorney.org/news/news/2026/May/castro-charges

entry.title: Lawsuit, Santa Clara County, near Gilroy, CA (2026-06-10)
entry.summary: California and Santa Clara County sued DHS and ICE to stop construction of a federally leased ICE facility on farmland near Gilroy (N.D. Cal.). Latest on record (2026-09-11): The court issued a preliminary injunction halting construction. Source: https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-bonta-county-santa-clara-sue-block-illegal-development-ice

entry.title: Lawsuit, Minneapolis and Saint Paul, MN (2026-01-12)
entry.summary: Minnesota, Minneapolis and Saint Paul sued DHS to stop Operation Metro Surge, a deployment of DHS agents, including ICE, to the Twin Cities (D. Minn.). Latest on record (2026-09-10): The court heard the federal government's motion to dismiss the case as moot on September 9, 2026; no ruling found. Source: https://ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2026/01/12_ICE.asp

entry.title: Lawsuit, New Jersey, NJ (2026-02-23)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued New Jersey over Executive Order No. 12, which bars civil immigration arrests in nonpublic areas of state property (United States v. New Jersey, D.N.J.). Latest on record (2026-09-04): The court dismissed the case; the executive order remains in effect. Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-files-lawsuit-against-new-jersey-interfering-federal-immigration-laws

entry.title: Lawsuit, Rochester, NY (2025-04-24)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued Rochester over its policy limiting city help with federal immigration enforcement (United States v. City of Rochester, W.D.N.Y.). Latest on record (2026-09-02): The court dismissed the amended complaint with prejudice and entered judgment for the city. Source: https://cityofrochester.gov/news/statement-mayor-city-council-president-city-rochester-regarding-legal-filing-us-department

entry.title: Lawsuit, Washtenaw County, MI (2026-04-09)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued Washtenaw County over its limits on cooperation with immigration authorities, on honoring ICE detainers and on federal agents' access to county property (E.D. Mich.). Latest on record (2026-08-21): The court dismissed the case, holding the county's policies are not overridden by federal law. Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-files-lawsuit-against-washtenaw-county-michigan-interfering-federal-0

entry.title: Lawsuit, 22 states, the District of Columbia and Pennsylvania's governor, led by Illinois, IL (2026-08-13)
entry.summary: States asked a federal court to quash a DHS immigration enforcement subpoena to the American Association of Motor Vehicle Administrators for about 17 million commercial driver's license records, including Social Security numbers (Illinois v. DHS, E.D. Va.). Latest on record (2026-08-20): The court put the motion on hold and extended the association's time to respond until further order. Source: https://ag.ny.gov/sites/default/files/court-filings/illinois-et-al-v-united-states-department-of-homeland-security-brief-iso-2026.pdf

entry.title: Criminal investigation, Minneapolis, MN (2026-01-09)
entry.summary: The Hennepin County Attorney and the Minnesota Attorney General opened a joint effort, including a public evidence portal, to gather evidence for a criminal investigation of a fatal shooting by an ICE officer in Minneapolis in January 2026. Latest on record (2026-08-20): No charges had been filed; the state investigation was continuing. Source: https://www.hennepinattorney.org/news/news/2026/January/HCAO-Evidence-Submission-Portal

entry.title: Lawsuit, New Mexico and Albuquerque, NM (2026-05-08)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued New Mexico and Albuquerque over a 2026 state law barring public bodies from contracting with ICE for detention and a city ordinance on ICE access (United States v. New Mexico, D.N.M.). Latest on record (2026-08-19): New Mexico filed counterclaims against the United States, DHS, ICE and Otero County seeking to void the county's 2026 detention agreement with ICE. Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-files-lawsuit-against-state-new-mexico-and-city-albuquerque-obstructing

entry.title: Lawsuit, States, led by California and Illinois, CA (2026-07-23)
entry.summary: States sued DHS and FEMA over 2026 grant conditions, including renewed requirements to help with civil immigration enforcement (D.R.I.). Source: https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-bonta-co-leads-lawsuit-challenging-trump-administration%E2%80%99s-0

entry.title: Lawsuit, Boston, MA (2025-09-04)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued Boston over its Trust Act and related policies that limit city help with federal immigration enforcement (United States v. City of Boston, D. Mass.). Latest on record (2026-07-23): The court dismissed the case for lack of standing on May 28, 2026; the United States appealed to the First Circuit. Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/department-justice-sues-city-boston-mayor-michelle-wu-over-sanctuary-city-laws

entry.title: Lawsuit, Minnesota, Minneapolis, Saint Paul and Hennepin County, MN (2025-09-29)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued Minnesota, Minneapolis, Saint Paul and Hennepin County over their policies on immigration detainers and data sharing (United States v. Minnesota, D. Minn.). Latest on record (2026-07-20): The court dismissed the case. Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-sues-minnesota-over-sanctuary-policies

entry.title: Lawsuit, Maryland, MD (2026-07-09)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued Maryland over its Community Trust Act and its handling of immigration detainers (D. Md.). Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-sues-maryland-over-sanctuary-policies

entry.title: Criminal charge, Milwaukee, WI (2025-04-24)
entry.summary: Federal prosecutors charged a Milwaukee County judge over her actions on April 18, 2025, when ICE officers came to her courthouse to arrest a defendant in her court. Latest on record (2026-07-09): A jury convicted her of obstructing a proceeding and acquitted her of concealment; she was fined $5,000 and appealed to the Seventh Circuit. Source: https://www.justice.gov/usao-edwi/pr/former-milwaukee-county-judge-sentenced-obstruction

entry.title: Lawsuit, Surprise, AZ (2026-04-24)
entry.summary: Arizona sued DHS and ICE over a proposed ICE detention facility in a Surprise warehouse (Arizona v. Mullin, D. Ariz.). Latest on record (2026-07-08): The case is paused by agreement; the federal side agreed not to hold people or begin conversion work there until its environmental review is complete. Source: https://www.azag.gov/press-release/attorney-general-mayes-sues-block-proposed-ice-detention-facility-surprise

entry.title: Lawsuit, Big Cypress (the state-run detention site known as Alligator Alcatraz), FL (2026-01-13)
entry.summary: In a brief to the Eleventh Circuit, the Miccosukee Tribe, a plaintiff in the suit since 2025, argued that the detention site harms its lands, water and cultural practices and that DHS and ICE must complete an environmental review (Friends of the Everglades v. Noem). Latest on record (2026-07-08): The Eleventh Circuit vacated the preliminary injunction that had halted the site, finding no final federal action. Source: https://indianz.com/News/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/13/miccosukee011326.pdf

entry.title: Order, letter or subpoena, Minnesota, Minneapolis and Saint Paul, MN (2026-01-20)
entry.summary: The Justice Department served grand jury subpoenas on Minnesota state, city and county officials in an investigation of alleged obstruction of immigration enforcement during Operation Metro Surge. Latest on record (2026-06-22): The federal court in Minnesota quashed the subpoenas. Source: https://ag.state.mn.us/Office/Communications/2026/06/22_Metro-Surge-Subpoenas.asp

entry.title: Lawsuit, Los Angeles, CA (2025-06-30)
entry.summary: The Justice Department sued Los Angeles over its ordinance barring the use of city resources for federal immigration enforcement (United States v. City of Los Angeles, C.D. Cal.). Latest on record (2026-06-20): The court granted the city's motion to dismiss. Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-department-files-lawsuit-against-sanctuary-city-policies-los-angeles-california

entry.title: Lawsuit, Romulus, MI (2026-03-24)
entry.summary: Michigan and Romulus sued DHS and ICE over ICE's plan to turn a Romulus warehouse into a detention center (E.D. Mich.). Latest on record (2026-06-18): ICE said it would sell the warehouse instead of using it for detention; the case stays open until a written agreement is made. Source: https://www.michigan.gov/ag/news/press-releases/2026/03/24/ag-nessel-files-lawsuit-challenging-plan-to-convert-romulus-warehouse-into-ice-detention-center

entry.title: Criminal charge, Logan, UT (2026-06-03)
entry.summary: A federal grand jury indicted two former Logan municipal court clerks on harboring, transporting and obstruction charges for allegedly leading people out a back door on April 9, 2026 while an ICE officer waited to make an arrest. Latest on record (2026-06-11): Both pleaded not guilty. Source: https://www.justice.gov/usao-ut/pr/two-former-utah-court-clerks-arrested-and-facing-federal-charges-after-allegedly-helping

entry.title: Criminal charge, New York City, NY (2025-09-18)
entry.summary: Federal officers arrested the New York City Comptroller at 26 Federal Plaza while he and state legislators were observing ICE holding areas, and he was charged federally. Latest on record (2026-06-11): A federal judge found him not guilty of a petty obstruction charge. Source: https://comptroller.nyc.gov/newsroom/statement-from-nyc-comptroller-brad-lander-on-proceeding-to-trial-for-september-18th-arrest-at-26-federal-plaza/
